title: Designing AI Learning Experiences for K-12: Emerging Works, Future Opportunities and a Design Framework
venue: Proceedings of the 2020 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems (CHI '20)
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the growing need for K-12-specific guidance on designing AI learning experiences. The authors note that although AI literacy is increasingly important, most prior AI literacy frameworks and learning tools were developed for general or older audiences and do not sufficiently account for the pedagogical, developmental, and practical constraints of school settings.

The paper does not test a new intervention. Instead, it conducts an exploratory review of 49 K-12 AI education works and tools, using Long and Magerko’s AI literacy framework as an analytic lens and extending it for K-12 contexts. The review covers AI curricula, classroom activities, tools, and learning experiences spanning elementary through high school, with some materials also involving teachers and parents. The authors code each work against AI literacy competencies and design considerations, then synthesize the findings into an educator-friendly reference chart and an extended design framework.

The main conclusions are that existing K-12 AI learning experiences often emphasize explainability, transparency, programming opportunities, and data contextualization, but under-address areas such as general-vs-narrow AI, interdisciplinarity, ethical reflection across all AI topics, gradual unveiling of complexity, identity and values, and parent support. The paper argues for more comprehensive AI literacy goals, built-in scaffolding, stronger engagement strategies, greater teacher and parent involvement, and deeper integration of AI into other school subjects.

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: Generic generative AI / conversational AI systems used by students, with no specific commercial product named.
identified_tools.use_case: Not directly evaluated in this paper. The paper is a conceptual/design-focused review of K-12 AI learning experiences and mentions generative AI only as one type of AI system in the literature.

quality_tier_rationale: This is an exploratory review and design-framework paper, not an empirical evaluation of a student-facing AI tool. It synthesizes prior K-12 AI education literature rather than reporting primary outcome data from a controlled study.
impact_tier_rationale: No direct tool impact is measured in this paper, so there is no empirical effect to score. The paper offers conceptual guidance and future opportunities, but not outcome evidence.
